sn46.2:1.2: For the phrase “sustained by food” see [dn33:1.8.2](), [an10.27:10.5](), [an10.28:4.5](), [kp4:1.2]() and notes.
sn46.2:1.3: The word _āhāra_, literally “intake”, may be translated as “food” or “fuel” depending on context.
sn46.2:2.2: “Feature of beauty” is _subhanimitta_. In early Pali, _nimitta_ is used for a feature or quality of the mind that, when focused on, promotes the growth of similar or related qualities. Thus focusing on beauty fosters the desire for that beauty. (See [mn5:6.1]()).
sn46.2:2.3: “Irrational” attention sees the beauty as something to be held on to and appropriated. The flaw lies not in the object, but in the response.
sn46.2:5.2: Worrying about anxiety makes the mind even more anxious.
sn46.2:6.2: Such as what the correct path is ([an3.65:3.8](), the various wrong views ([sn24.1:5.1]()), the status of a saint after death ([sn44.9:5.2](), or the reality of kamma ([sn42.13:21.2]()).
